core_findings: Human causation of contemporary global warming is unequivocal; the causal evidence is physical and attribution-based, not a simple time-series correlation.
Cumulative CO2 is the cleanest emissions-to-temperature dashboard relationship: best estimate 0.45 C per 1,000 GtCO2, likely 0.27-0.63 C.
Every additional increment of warming raises hazards; extreme heat shows one of the clearest and strongest temperature-conditioned responses.
Tropical cyclones are expected to become wetter and more intense on average, while total global frequency decreases or remains approximately unchanged.
Biodiversity risk rises steeply with warming, but climate operates alongside land/sea-use change, exploitation, pollution, and invasive species.
Food impacts are crop- and context-specific; climate has slowed productivity growth, but crop yield is not identical to food security.
Freshwater risk is about availability, timing, reliability, quality, and extremes—not disappearance of a fixed global freshwater stock.
Sea-level rise is observed, accelerating, human-driven, and committed for centuries to millennia; global values require localization before community use.
Climate-related displacement is real and increasing in importance, but no defensible global climate-refugees-per-degree coefficient exists.
